items.title: Claremont author faces criticism over AI art in new book
items.excerpt: Claremont Middle School hosted author Giulio Savo and his book "Directive Detectives: The Freedom Trail Directive," sparking debate over the use of AI in children's literature.
items.rationale: Fresh, concrete local case of AI illustration backlash in children's books; strong original photo.

items.title: OpenAI seeks to exclude book market study, citing funding ties to authors' law firm
items.excerpt: The accuracy and funding of research claiming Gen AI causes market harm have become important questions in the consolidated lawsuits.
items.rationale: New filing in the consolidated authors-v-OpenAI case targeting the market-harm evidence authors rely on.

items.title: Is AI coming for audiobooks?
items.excerpt: AI companies like ElevenLabs and Spoken are angling for the fast-growing audiobook market. It remains to be seen if consumers will buy in.
items.rationale: Mainstream business reporting on ElevenLabs and Spoken pushing into audiobooks, with consumer-demand angle.

items.title: Faster Chat, Better Rewrite & Printing
items.excerpt: Sudowrite's Chat responses are now twice as fast, with an improved Rewrite tool and new printing support for manuscripts.
items.rationale: Actionable writing-tool feature release (2x Chat, better Rewrite, printing), distinct from the 09-28 model-addition card.

items.title: AI might kill us, but is that so bad?
items.excerpt: While the advent of AI has alarmed most writers, Bonnie Garmus argues it has also shone a light on the hubris of humankind.
items.rationale: Bestselling novelist Bonnie Garmus (Lessons in Chemistry) weighs in on AI and writers; the strongest remaining fresh, on-topic books item after duplicates were excluded.

https://janefriedman.com/openai-seeks-to.new_action: New OpenAI filing (motion to exclude the authors' book-market-harm study, citing its funding ties to plaintiffs' law firm) in the consolidated case.

SWAP (2026-10-03, orchestrator request): removed The Digital Reader 'Can Better Wording Fix the "Made With AI" Problem?' because the fetched article carries a paid/sponsored link insertion on a link-farm site and the research concerns advertising labels, not books. Replacement: Bookseller 'AI might kill us, but is that so bad?' (Bonnie Garmus comment, 10-01). It is opinion, but no concrete-news candidate survived: the remaining ones were either duplicates (ROSS, LibGen, AI-use report, Sudowrite models, possible Orelien repeat) or off-topic or thin (Dartmouth provost is higher-ed governance; the Frankfurt program preview overlaps PW's 09-25 Frankfurt preview and has little AI angle). The Garmus essay matches no published story: the nearest Bookseller comment pieces (09-17 emails, 09-29 secrecy, 10-02 narration) argue different points. It takes the freed accent #2ec5c5.
